policies.title: Endangered Species Act: habitat harm, threatened-species rules, and regulatory reversals
policies.status: 2026 final rules effective; separate listing and consultation proposals pending in current agency materials; later litigation not fully audited
policies.summary: ESA regulations repeatedly changed legal protection for listed species and habitat. These are conservation policies with implications for individual animals, not direct measures of suffering or survival.
policies.changed: The scope of habitat-related take, default protections for future threatened species, habitat-exclusion procedures, and listing and consultation rules changed at different times.
policies.afterward: The 2026 harm rescission and FWS revisions reached final-rule status. Other proposed revisions must be evaluated separately.
policies.attribution: Congress supplied the statute. FWS, NMFS and DOI made administrative changes under Trump I, Biden and Trump II. Obama-era habitat policy and the Clinton-era Sweet Home judgment are background; a court judgment is not presidential executive credit.
policies.unknown: No causal estimate of deaths, injuries, suffering, extinction risk, or habitat loss attributable to these reversals was established in this bounded review.
policies.mechanism: Listing, take prohibitions, threatened-species protective rules, and consultation over federal actions.
policies.coverage: Listed species and designated habitat, with different provisions for wildlife, plants, threatened species and federal actions.
policies.exceptions: Permits and species-specific rules matter. Existing threatened-species protections survive the 2026 blanket-rule change. Removing the regulatory harm definition does not repeal the ESA.
policies.confidenceReason: High confidence in retrieved rule text; lower confidence in complete litigation status and no independently estimated animal-welfare effect.

contributors.role: Regulations and implementation within their jurisdictions
Statutory interpretation and review of agency actions

history.event: Sweet Home upheld the prior definition covering habitat modification that actually kills or injures wildlife.
Trump I revised listing and consultation regulations and removed FWS's blanket option for future threatened listings; existing blanket protection remained.
FWS adopted habitat-exclusion procedures superseding its 2016 policy; Biden rescinded those regulations on July 21, 2022.
Biden restored the blanket option and revised listing and consultation rules, effective May 6. Listing text again expressly excluded economic impacts from listing determinations.
FWS and NMFS proposed rescinding their harm definitions; proposal publication itself changed no operative regulation.
Trump II proposed four additional ESA regulatory revisions.
Agencies finalized harm-definition removal from 50 CFR 17.3 and 222.102.
FWS finalized future blanket-option removal and revised habitat-exclusion procedures.
FWS still categorizes separate listing and interagency-cooperation revisions as proposed.

policies.title: Migratory Bird Treaty Act: incidental-take reversals
species: Migratory birds protected by the MBTA
policies.status: DOI exclusion interpretation restored in 2025 with explicit Southern District of New York exception; implementation corroborated May 2026
policies.summary: Successive administrations reversed whether accidental bird killing falls within the agency's MBTA interpretation. This changed a prevention and enforcement tool; the resulting mortality effect is unmeasured here.
policies.changed: Agency legal interpretations, a temporary regulation, enforcement guidance, and a proposed authorization initiative changed separately.
policies.afterward: FWS confirms implementation of the 2025 reversal; no comparable national enforcement or mortality series was verified for this policy.
policies.attribution: Obama DOI reaffirmed broad coverage; Trump I DOI narrowed it and promulgated a rule. Biden withdrew the opinion and revoked the rule. Trump II restored the opinion. Courts independently constrained interpretation.
policies.unknown: How changes affected preventive industry behavior, enforcement, mortality, or suffering, after accounting for hazard exposure, technology and other laws.
policies.mechanism: Legal liability and agency enforcement concerning incidental injury or killing.
policies.coverage: Birds covered by the MBTA and relevant conduct; this is a conservation statute rather than a comprehensive individual-animal welfare standard.
policies.exceptions: Permits, judicial precedent, and enforcement discretion matter. The 2025 memorandum expressly excepts reliance within SDNY jurisdiction.
policies.confidenceReason: Primary rules, memoranda and a court opinion verify chronology; no full post-May-2026 litigation audit or causal outcomes estimate.

history.event: Obama's M-37041 reaffirmed the longstanding agency view that incidental take is prohibited.
Trump I's M-37050 reversed that position.
SDNY vacated M-37050 and remanded to DOI.
Trump I codified incidental-take exclusion; the corrected effective date was March 8, 2021.
Biden's M-37065 withdrew M-37050 after the government's appeal was dismissed March 2.
Biden revoked the January rule effective December 3 and separately initiated rulemaking on incidental-take authorization.
Trump II's M-37085 withdrew M-37065 and restored reliance on M-37050 with the SDNY exception.
FWS withdrew the 2021 incidental-take authorization advance notice.
FWS confirmed the restored interpretation, withdrawn advance notice and rescinded Director's Order 225.

claims.claim: Sweet Home upheld the earlier habitat-related harm definition; the 2026 rescission is an agency action, not a Supreme Court reversal of that decision.
claims.limitations: Does not resolve later challenges to the rescission.

claims.claim: The 2024 rules revised portions of the 2019 listing and consultation framework and restored the FWS blanket protection option. They did not repeal every 2019 provision.
claims.limitations: Framework changes do not themselves establish improved welfare.

claims.claim: The April 2025 harm proposal became a July 14, 2026 final rule, effective September 14. It removes regulatory definitions, while harm remains in the statutory definition of take.
claims.locator: 91 FR43300 Dates and Background; final amendments
claims.limitations: Judicial interpretation and enforcement remain material; no claim that all habitat destruction became lawful.

claims.claim: Effective August 20, 2026, FWS removed the future blanket-rule option, preserving existing threatened-species protections. Species-specific rules remain available; removal does not mean every newly threatened species lacks protection.
claims.limitations: FWS rule, not a change to NMFS's separate threatened-species program.

claims.claim: The 2026 critical-habitat exclusion procedure is final; separate listing and consultation revisions are still described as proposals on the current FWS status page.
claims.locator: 91 FR45662 Dates; status page Final Rules / Proposed Rules
claims.evidenceType: Final rule and agency status page
claims.limitations: Status-page freshness and later court orders require continued checking.

claims.claim: Obama's January 2017 opinion endorsed incidental-take coverage. Trump I reversed the interpretation, and the Southern District of New York vacated that opinion in August 2020.
claims.locator: Court opinion background and conclusion; 86 FR1134
claims.limitations: Circuit interpretations differ; this is not a Supreme Court holding.

claims.claim: Trump I's January 2021 regulation excluded incidental take. Biden revoked it effective December 3, 2021, returning to incidental-take coverage subject to judicial precedent and enforcement discretion.
claims.limitations: No standardized mortality counterfactual is established by these rules.

claims.claim: M-37085 reinstates the 2017 exclusion interpretation as binding within DOI, except actions relying on it within the Southern District of New York's jurisdiction.
claims.limitations: Agency interpretation does not amend the statute or settle conflicting judicial interpretations.

claims.claim: Trump II withdrew the 2021 advance notice for incidental-take authorization; FWS's May 2026 presentation also reports rescission of Director's Order 225.
claims.evidenceType: Withdrawal notice and agency implementation report
claims.limitations: The advance notice was a rulemaking initiative, not an operational general permit program.

gaps.topic: Conservation is not a welfare outcome
gaps.detail: No policy-specific causal mortality, injury or suffering estimate is supported by this legal chronology.

gaps.impact: No lives-saved total, welfare effect size or presidential ranking.
